items.title: Neo-Nazi Thomas Sewell broadcasting hate on Instagram from Victorian acreage
items.description: ABC NEWS Verify can reveal that Neo-Nazi leader Thomas Sewell has been uploading antisemitic and homophobic diatribes to Instagram from a property on the outskirts of Melbourne.

items.title: ABS estimates 80pc of tobacco consumed in Australia last year was illegally sourced
items.description: The experimental estimates are based on "nicotine metabolite concentrations" detected in wastewater samples, combined with data showing a collapse in spending on legal cigarettes and vapes.

items.title: Another KPMG leader steps aside amid audit leak scandal fallout
items.description: KPMG Australia chief operating officer Eileen Hoggett will step aside from her role while investigations are pending into the audit leak scandal at the big four firm.

items.title: Parents of fit 27-year-old asked what quality of life he had by medical staff
items.description: Sam Stubbs’s parents were asked about his quality of life while treating him for a lung infection. They realised it was because he was born with Down syndrome.

items.title: How one optimal AUKUS submarine pathway became two
items.description: Scrutiny of AUKUS's delivery reveals two "optimal pathways" for Australia's submarines.

items.title: Defence plans to sell Sydney Harbour land Albanese once fought to protect
items.description: Parliamentary speeches from 2021 reveal the prime minister was opposed to privatising Sydney Harbour land now being sold off by the Defence Department.

items.title: Australia's economy growing at 2.5 per cent annually as slowdown begins
items.description: Australia's economy grew at an annual rate of 2.5 per cent in the March quarter, the same as in the previous quarter.

items.title: New Solomon Islands leader wants to 'reset' relations with Australia
items.description: The new Solomon Islands PM has made a clear pivot towards Australia, agreeing to kickstart negotiations on a comprehensive treaty and promising to "review" the Pacific nation's contentious security agreement with China.

items.title: These are the 'worst offenders' in Australian packaging
items.description: A trendy plastic-and-metal takeaway cup used by cafes for iced drinks has been named Australia's worst packaging in the first Unpackit Awards.

items.title: 'Too dangerous to push ahead': Aussie diver leaves Laos cave rescue
items.description: Josh Richards is on his way back to Australia, after multiple days helping rescue miners trapped in a Laos cave.

items.title: 'You broke a tradition': Man fined for booing during Welcome to Country
items.description: Eli Toby told the court that his actions were intended as a way to "stand for what I believed was the right thing at the time", but refused to apologise to the judge.

items.title: Police investigating people entering New York sewers for unknown reason
items.description: Security cameras have recorded at least three night time instances where groups of people entered or exited sewer tunnels via maintenance holes on streets in Brooklyn and Queens.

items.title: Iran launches ballistic missiles at American base as US hits Qeshm Island
items.description: The Revolutionary Guard says it has fired missiles and drones at US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain, while the US military has launched an attack on Qeshm Island.

items.title: Gold reserves grow at Kalgoorlie's Super Pit
items.description: A big exploration push by Australia's biggest gold miner, Northern Star Resources, has grown the reserves at the Super Pit by 54 per cent in the past six years.

items.title: Five ways to prevent mould in your home and the best ways to clean it
items.description: Winter is here and with it comes the increased risk of mould in homes, particularly in colder parts of the country. But there are simple ways to keep to it at bay.

items.title: Hollywood legend set to bring Finke Desert Race to the big screen
items.description: The gruelling outback Finke Desert Race is set for Hollywood treatment after Marvel's Chris Hemsworth backs a feature-length movie.

items.title: Why Hugh Jackman's brother cried on his first day as a prison-school teacher
items.description: After Ralph Jackman retrained as a teacher, his first job was in a youth detention centre. His new memoir reveals how a broken system is failing vulnerable kids.

items.title: Singer known for Disney's Aladdin hit duet A Whole New World dies
items.description: Peabo Bryson, known for his Grammy and Oscar-winning Disney collaborations, has died at 75.

items.title: Underworld figure Mick Gatto released without charge following arrest
items.description: Mick Gatto has been released without charge after being arrested by Victorian police investigating "alleged financial offences" earlier today.

items.title: 'Perverse logic' over abortion, Barnaby Joyce tells Sydney crowd
items.description: Nine months out from the NSW election campaign, One Nation recruit Barnaby Joyce has appeared in Sydney, declaring politicians are fearful of losing their jobs.

items.title: Dramatic daylight arrest of NT man with police shooting front tyre of vehicle
items.description: Northern Territory police have carried out a dramatic arrest of a 33-year-old man on a main Darwin road, saying the fugitive was wanted for a breach of parole.

items.title: Border Force busts NT multi-million-dollar illicit tobacco operation
items.description: Australian Border Force officers have seized hundreds of thousands of illegal cigarettes and vapes worth millions of dollars from a Northern Territory storage facility.

items.title: 'Us duck hunters': Victorian watchdog accused of siding with shooters
items.description: The Game Management Authority is accused of turning a blind eye to illegal behaviour by shooters while bullying wildlife rescuers and anti-hunting campaigners.

items.title: Starmer condemns handcuffed teen's death as police response sparks protests
items.description: The British prime minister said he "felt sick" while watching video released by police of 18-year-old Henry Nowak, who was handcuffed while he lay dying from stab wounds after his killer falsely alleged a racist attack.

items.title: Trump names inexperienced ally as intelligence director
items.description: Bill Pulte, who is known for publicly attacking the US president's political enemies, would also retain his existing jobs overseeing federal housing and mortgage policies.
